summary: The Regenerate step provenance (cinatra#4264, slice B1a). Adds artifact_materializations.verified_step_id (text, nullable: the runtime's signed id of the ApiNode that filed the revision, written only when it equals the claim's node_id), the index artifact_materializations_org_artifact_rev_idx on (org_id, artifact_id, representation_revision_id) WHERE path = 'materialize_tool', the table agent_run_step_snapshots (org_id, run_id REFERENCES agent_runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, node_id, inputs_json, inputs_sha256, flow_sha256, ambiguous, created_at; PRIMARY KEY (run_id, node_id)), lifecycle_repair.regenerate_node_id, source_artifact_id and source_representation_revision_id (text, nullable), and the index lifecycle_repair_successor_idx on (successor_artifact_id, successor_representation_revision_id). Additive: no backfill, no stored value changes, every existing row reads NULL; snapshots are removed with their run, a template purge included. up runs outside a transaction (noTransaction): the two indexes are built CONCURRENTLY, an INVALID index of the same name left by a failed build is dropped first, and every lock wait is bounded by lock_timeout 5 s (set first, reset last), so a wait fails (55P03) and replays. Idempotent up. Fresh-install bootstrap twins in artifactMaterializationLedgerSchemaQueries, agentRunStepSnapshotSchemaQueries and lifecycleRepairSchemaQueries ship in the same change. down is DATA-DESTRUCTIVE: it drops the table, both indexes and the four columns, losing every step snapshot, verified filing step and Regenerate intent; those revisions are refused Regenerate afterwards.
